questions.text: How is Black soil different from Red soil? What are the differences between Black soil and Red Soil?
questions.text_as_printed: How is Black soil different from Red soil? What are the differences between Black soil and Red Soil? (Difficult)

answer.value:
Black Soil
Black soil is also called ‘Regur soil’.
It is best suited for cotton cultivation.
It is also called ‘Black Cotton soil’.
Formed from the weathering of igneous rock.
It contains more of clay particles.
It is fertile and capable of retaining water.
This type of soil is seen in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Western areas of Andhra Pradesh and North Karnataka.
It is highly suitable for dry farming.
Cotton, jowar, wheat, onion, chilly, tobacco, oil seeds, lemon and grapes are the major crops growing in this soil.
Red Soil.
Largest area of peninsular Plateau covered with red soil.
It can be seen from Kanyakumari in the South to Jhansi in the North.
It spreads from Gujarat’s Kutch area to Raj Mahal hills in the Jharkhand area.
The major crops growing in this type of soil are ragi, tobacco and oil seeds.
Having irrigation facility grow paddy, sugarcane, cotton etc.
